clue.text: Notes made on staff

parts.note: the staff is the ... stave, the five lines on which notes are written, not a company's employees

explanation.surface: Memos jotted down about the employees of a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' reads as a workforce, but it is the stave of written music, so the notes are musical ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Written notation placed on a stave is what a composer produces as a score.

clue.text: Villain involved in arms etc.

indicators.note: involved, meaning tangled up, says the letters are mixed

parts.note: the nine letters of the phrase are the fodder

explanation.surface: A villain mixed up in weapons dealing and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges IN ARMS ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or scoundrel is a villain.

clue.text: Put away — in other words, no longer available

parts.note: sc, scilicet, means namely or that is to say
a dish that is off is no longer on the menu

explanation.surface: Food eaten up, in other words none left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' is slang for eat greedily. SC (scilicet) means 'namely', 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat food greedily is to wolf it down.

clue.text: Fear to gamble after business dispute

indicators.note: after places the gamble behind the business and dispute

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
war is a dispute or conflict
to dice is to gamble

explanation.surface: Fear of risking money after a quarrel at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fear' is the definition, a noun here; the clue's order of business and dispute matches the answer's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of courage is a state of fear.

clue.text: It's wearable, and possibly throwable

indicators.note: possibly says the following word may be rearranged into something else

parts.note: the nine letters of the word are the fodder

explanation.surface: An item one can both wear and hurl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges THROWABLE into the hat; a bowler also throws in cricket, which gives the surface its wit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard round felt hat is an item of headgear one puts on.

clue.text: Group of soldiers ordered to hide equipment

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: bade means ordered
a rig is equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: Soldiers told to conceal their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a description of the soldiers but supplies the past tense of bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit of several battalions is a group of soldiers.

clue.text: Fight involving welterweights of no importance

indicators.note: involving, taken as twisting up, says the remaining letters are mixed
of no says the word for importance is removed

parts.note: weight means importance

explanation.surface: A bout between welterweights that counts for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove WEIGHT ('of no importance') from WELTERWEIGHTS to leave WELTERS, which 'involving' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with an opponent is to fight.

clue.text: Force out ace, moving right to left

indicators.note: right to left says RT, the abbreviation for right, is replaced by L for left

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An ace is pushed out, moving from right to left.
explanation.walkthrough: RT is right and L is left: swap them in EXPERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to drive out by force.

clue.text: Sewing kit for home economist

definitions.meaning: a small case of needles and thread, pronounced hussif
a woman running a household, jokingly an economist of the home

explanation.surface: A sewing kit suitable for a domestic science teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The old word for a needle case is spelt like the word for a homemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket needlework case had this name, and so does a woman managing a household.

clue.text: Drink tea, say? All right

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, giving a letter of the same sound

parts.note: tea is said the same as the letter T
okay means all right

explanation.surface: Offering someone tea and checking that is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea, say' gives the letter T. The drink is not tea but a sweet Hungarian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet Hungarian wine is a drink.

clue.text: Pure and animated heroine

definitions.meaning: spotless, as white as fresh snowfall
the princess of Disney's first full-length cartoon film

explanation.surface: A cartoon heroine of unblemished virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means flawlessly white, and the fairy-tale princess starred in the 1937 Disney cartoon.

clue.text: Yank's spirit

definitions.meaning: to yank is to pull sharply, as at a string or feather
spirit here is courage or nerve

explanation.surface: Describing the plucky character of an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is a verb meaning to tug; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull sharply at something is to tug it, and courage or nerve is grit.

clue.text: 13 engineers backed judge

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: backed says the word for judge is written in reverse order

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: Engineers support a judge in some numbered matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 13 stands for the answer to 13 across, the verb meaning to attribute.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something to a source is to credit it to that source.

clue.text: Guns I will put in vessel

indicators.note: put in says one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: an artery is a blood vessel
I will contracts to I'll

explanation.surface: Someone promising to load guns aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy guns collectively form an army's cannon or ordnance.

clue.text: Attribute of a writer

parts.note: a scribe is one who writes or copies documents

explanation.surface: A quality belonging to an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attribute' looks like a noun but is the verb, to credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something is to credit it to a source.

clue.text: Be persuaded to visit

definitions.meaning: to change one's mind and agree

explanation.surface: Someone talked into calling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to change opinion, and also to drop by someone's home.

clue.text: National side in American game

definitions.meaning: belonging to the nation of England
in American pool or billiards, side is the spin put on the cue ball

explanation.surface: A country's team playing in a US sport.
explanation.walkthrough: In American billiards, spin put on the ball is called english, a term little known in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names something of England, and Americans call spin on a billiard ball by this word.

clue.text: Activity resulting from original job creation scheme

definitions.text: Activity resulting from original job creation scheme

parts.words: Activity resulting from original job creation scheme
parts.note: the original job is Adam's in Eden, given at the Creation, tending the plants

explanation.surface: Work produced by an early government employment programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'job creation scheme' suggests politics, but it is the Creation in Genesis, where Adam was put in Eden to tend it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending plants was the first task assigned to man in Genesis.

clue.text: Churchmen put in that special decoration on tomb

indicators.note: put in says one piece goes inside the other
special, meaning made specially, says the word is rearranged

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church, followed by men

explanation.surface: Clergy installing an unusual ornament on a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' is the anagram signal; 'Churchmen' splits into the usual church abbreviation plus men. The decoration is a panel of a dead person's coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond-shaped armorial panel is displayed for the dead, often in church near a grave.

clue.text: Encountered recurrent problem with plants in bad weather

indicators.note: recurrent, read as running back, says the word is written backwards

parts.note: met means encountered
a pest is an insect or creature damaging plants

explanation.surface: A gardener met repeated trouble with plants during storms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurrent' turns MET into TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent storm is bad weather.

clue.text: Such a dancer swept Dorothy off her feet

definitions.meaning: one who does the Twist, a 1960s dance
in The Wizard of Oz, a tornado carries Dorothy away

explanation.surface: A dancer who sweeps a girl off her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swept off her feet' sounds romantic but is the tornado in The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: A Twist dancer gets the name, as does an American tornado, which literally lifted the heroine of Oz.

clue.text: Snake's done in queen, when clasped

indicators.note: clasped says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: done in means exhausted, spent
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A snake is killed by a queen who has it in her grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done in' suggests killed but means tired out, SPENT, which grips ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reptile without limbs is a serpent, a literary term for one.

clue.text: United Nations brought in to secure hot spot

indicators.note: brought in to says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to strap is to secure

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers sent to secure a trouble spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot spot' suggests a conflict zone, but it is a sheltered sunny place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered sunny corner of a garden is a hot spot.

clue.text: An acorn — it can develop into a plant

indicators.note: develop says the letters before grow into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An acorn has the potential to grow into a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can develop into' rearranges AN ACORN and IT; the plant is not an oak but a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove pink is a flowering garden plant.

clue.text: Animal — shy cat — losing mother

parts.note: coy means shy

indicators.note: losing says a part is taken away from the cat

parts.note: a puma is a big cat
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A timid cat has been separated from its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: PUMA loses MA, leaving PU.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American rodent, also called nutria, is an animal.

clue.text: Shudder at injuries inflicted on soldiers

parts.note: ABH is actual bodily harm, a British legal term for injury
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Horror at the wounds suffered by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH is actual bodily harm, a criminal charge in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to recoil from it in disgust.

clue.text: One must turn to part of Bible to find him

indicators.note: must turn says the word is written backwards

parts.note: CH, chapter, is part of a Bible book

explanation.surface: A believer must consult Scripture to discover someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must turn' gives ENO; 'him' is the definition, a biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The father of Methuselah is an Old Testament man, here referred to as a pronoun.

clue.text: Harangue half the voters

indicators.note: half says only part of the word is kept

parts.note: the electorate is the voters

explanation.surface: Lecturing half of the electorate.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first half of ELECTORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a pompous speech is to harangue.

clue.text: Some carry out handiwork in early life

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Children doing crafts at an early age.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'in', but the answer is a noun; 'in' is the link word and 'early life' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The early years of a person are the period of being young.

clue.text: Stop administering sodium to insect

indicators.note: administering sodium to the insect puts the element inside it

parts.note: a termite is an insect
NA is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: Stop giving the insect sodium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'administering' reads as giving a dose but here simply puts the sodium symbol into the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something to an end is to stop it.

clue.text: Support from below, bringing European articles forward

definitions.text: Support from below, bringing European articles forward

indicators.note: bringing with forward says a piece is moved to the front
forward says the piece goes to the front of the word

parts.note: a prop is a support
under means below
UN is a French article and DER a German one

explanation.surface: Propping up while promoting some continental items.
explanation.walkthrough: PROP UNDER is support from below; the articles UN and DER spell UNDER, so 'bringing ... forward' puts them first.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up is to brace a thing from beneath.

clue.text: Visitor supposed to be seen but not heard? On the contrary

indicators.note: heard, after the reversal of the saying, says the word is spoken

parts.note: supposed means guessed

explanation.surface: Like children, a visitor should be seen and not heard, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Children 'should be seen and not heard'; on the contrary, the answer is heard but not seen as GUESSED, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone staying in your home is a visitor.
